vehicles.speed_basis: Normal top speed of 40 km/h from the Battlefield 4 infobox on the Battlefield Wiki M1 Abrams page ('40 KPH Standard; 56 KPH Max'). The 56 km/h figure is the driver's speed boost and is not used.
vehicles.note: This is the anchor tank. Under method B its ratio is 1.0 by definition, which I banded medium (see unclear on the shared 1.0 boundary). With the boost (15.56 m/s) the bands would not change: A is 2.39 (fast) and B is 1.40 (medium). The BF4 T-90A and Type 99 infoboxes give the same 40/56 km/h.

vehicles.speed_basis: Normal top speed of 42 km/h from the Battlefield 4 infobox on the Battlefield Wiki LAV-25 page ('42 km/h, 65 km/h (boost), 28 km/h (in water)'). Boost not used.
vehicles.note: The wiki says wheeled IFVs may reach a higher top speed than tracked tanks, but the normal figure is only 2 km/h above the Abrams. The boost changes the band under both methods: 65 km/h (18.06 m/s) gives A = 2.78 (very fast) and B = 1.63 (fast). The BTR-90 and ZBD-09 BF4 infoboxes give 42/65 and 42/64 km/h.

vehicles.speed_basis: No figure found. The Battlefield Wiki's BF4 infobox (Growler ITV page) gives no speed, only maneuverability 'Fast' and 'Fast attack vehicle'. Its BF3 section, the VDV Buggy and LYT2021 counterparts, and web searches give no in-game km/h either. The page's real-world note (105 km/h) is not a game figure.
vehicles.note: Judged from its role and from figures for neighbouring vehicles. It is BF4's fast attack buggy, clearly faster than the IFVs (42 km/h, 65 boosted) and the Tunguska (0-65 KPH in its BF4 infobox). The BF3 Dirt Bike page gives 95 km/h. Band A is very fast for anything above 58.5 km/h, so it is firm. Band B is fast for roughly 60-100 km/h and very fast above 100 km/h (2.5 x 40), so it depends on a number I could not find. I assumed about 80-100 km/h.

vehicles.speed_basis: 330 km/h from the Battlefield 3 infobox on the Battlefield Wiki AH-1Z Viper page, used as a proxy. The BF4 infobox on the same page gives no speed.
vehicles.note: The raw figure comes from another title. Other wiki hints: the BF4 UH-1Y Venom infobox lists 360 km/h; the Attack Aircraft page says BF4 attack jets are about 240 km/h, down from 321 in BF3; the BF4 Viper text says only that the Viper and Havoc are faster than the Z-10W. A ludo.guide figure of 410 km/h matches the real aircraft (about 411 km/h), so I did not use it. Both bands are very fast for any plausible value: even 150 km/h gives A = 6.4 and B = 3.75.

vehicles.speed_basis: 66 km/h on level ground with no upgrades, from the Steam community 'Tank guide' (posted Feb 2018, updated Oct 2020). The PS2 wiki gives no figure; its infobox says only 'a higher top speed' than the other tanks. Racer chassis not counted.
vehicles.note: This is the anchor tank, so B is 1.0 by definition. The figure is a dated community value, not the wiki's. A planetsideguide.com snippet in search results gives 79 km/h with the Racer chassis; I could not open the page, which is offline. Band A would fall to fast if the stock top speed were under 58.5 km/h, which is unlikely: the same guide gives the slower Vanguard 60 km/h.

vehicles.speed_basis: About 70 km/h on level ground, from the same Steam 'Tank guide' (2018, updated 2020). The PS2 wiki (Lightning/Main) gives no number but says the Lightning is 'faster, more maneuverable and smaller' than the MBTs. Stock, no Racer chassis.
vehicles.note: Band B rests on the wiki's description as well as the number. Faster than the MBTs but nowhere near 1.5x (99 km/h) puts it in medium, just above 1.0. A 2014 video description in search results gives about 70 km/h forward with the Rival chassis.

vehicles.speed_basis: 90 km/h unupgraded, from the Steam community guide 'The Harasser' (posted 2013, updated May 2025). The same guide gives 110 km/h with max Racer chassis. Turbo bursts are not counted. The PS2 wiki gives no number; Harasser/Main mentions 'high speed' and a turbo for 'a large burst of speed'.
vehicles.note: Band B sits fairly close to the 1.5 boundary (99 km/h). Max Racer chassis (110 km/h) gives B = 1.67 (fast), and turbo would too. The 90 km/h figure dates from 2013, so later patches may have moved it. The wiki's Vehicle Gears page mentions a gear ceiling at about 40 km/h in a Harasser, which shows the speedometer is the right way to measure. Band A is very fast either way.

vehicles.speed_basis: No figure found. The PS2 wiki (Sunderer/Main) gives none. 'The Complete Sunderer Guide' on Steam (2014) says it is 'only beaten in speed by the Lightning tank and the Harrasser buggy on even ground' but turns badly. The wiki says Racer and Rival chassis were built into the base Sunderer in the July 9, 2024 update.
vehicles.note: Judged as roughly MBT speed or slightly above, about 66-75 km/h. That gives A of about 2.8-3.2 (very fast) and B of about 1.0-1.15 (medium). If it is actually a little slower than the Prowler on the flat, B would be slow. The source is old (2014), and the 2024 built-in Racer chassis may have raised the speed, but not past 1.5x the Prowler (99 km/h).

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed of 5.42 m/s from the Foxhole Wiki (wiki.gg) Silverhand - Mk. IV infobox ('offspeed'). Road speed 7.75 not used. Matches the wiki's Movement Speed table.
vehicles.note: This is the anchor tank. The soldier walks at 5 m/s (Movement Speed page), so in Foxhole methods A and B differ only by a factor of 1.084. Sprinting at full stamina is about 7.2 m/s, which would make A 0.75 (slow).

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed of 5.79 m/s from the Foxhole Wiki Devitt Mk. III infobox. Road speed 8.27 not used.
vehicles.note: The light tank is only 7% faster than the assault tank off road, so both methods put it in the same band as the Silverhand. The Movement Speed table gives the same 8.27/5.79.

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed of 3.27 m/s from the Foxhole Wiki O'Brien V.110 infobox and its Engine & Mobility text ('10.88m/s on road, 3.27m/s off-road').
vehicles.note: The armoured car uses truck mobility, so off road it is slower than a walking soldier, and the off-road rule makes it very slow. On road (10.88) it would be fast under A (2.18) and medium under B if compared with the tank's road speed (1.40 vs 7.75). The wiki calls its off-road speed 'mediocre'. The number is certain; whether the band reflects how the vehicle is used is not.

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed of 3.46 m/s from the Foxhole Wiki Dunne Transport infobox and Engine & Mobility text ('17.32m/s on road, 3.46m/s off-road'). This is the unloaded (0% encumbrance) value; the Movement Speed table gives 3.46 / 2.77 / 2.49 for 0% / 1-99% / 100%+ load.
vehicles.note: Band A is 0.692, just under the 0.7 line. Petrol (+10%, Movement Speed page) would give 3.81 m/s, A = 0.76 (slow). Loaded, A is 0.55. On road the truck is the fastest vehicle here (17.32 m/s: A = 3.46, very fast). Like the O'Brien, the off-road rule turns a road logistics vehicle into a very slow one.

unclear: 1) Boundaries. 'Slow' is '0.7 to 1' and 'medium' is '1 to 1.5', so both claim exactly 1.0. Every anchor tank under method B lands on that line. I assigned it to medium, reading the bands as very-slow <0.7, slow 0.7 to <1.0, medium 1.0-1.5, fast >1.5-2.5, very-fast >2.5; '0.7' and '1.5' are inclusive for the lower band as well. The vocabulary should say so explicitly. 2) What method B does. For BF and PS2 ground vehicles it does spread them out: under A nearly everything is fast or very fast; under B the tanks, IFV, Lightning, Harasser and Sunderer are medium and the buggy is fast. Aircraft divided by a 40 km/h tank give ratios of 6-8+, so all air ends up very fast under either method; B gives no separation in the air layer, and an air anchor may be needed. Under A, PS2's 66 km/h MBT is already 'very fast' (2.82) while the BF4 MBT is 'fast' (1.71), so the same archetype bands differently between games; B removes that. 3) Foxhole off-road rule. It makes wheeled vehicles (O'Brien 3.27, Dunne 3.46 m/s) slower than a walking soldier, so they band very slow under both methods, although on road they are the fastest units (Dunne 17.32 m/s). If the band is meant to describe operational mobility, road speed or a mixed figure may fit better; if it is meant to describe battlefield manoeuvre, off-road is defensible. Foxhole also compares a walking soldier with sprint references in BF and PS2. 4) Which 'normal' speed to use. BF4 vehicles have a driver boost, and the LAV-25 changes band under both methods depending on whether boost counts (A fast to very fast, B medium to fast). PS2 speeds depend on Racer chassis rank (Harasser 90 vs 110 km/h moves B from medium to fast), and since July 2024 the Sunderer has Racer built in. Foxhole speeds depend on encumbrance (the infobox gives the empty value) and on fuel type (petrol +10%). I used stock, unboosted, unupgraded, unloaded, diesel figures. 5) Evidence quality and the 'judged' flag. The PS2 wiki has no vehicle speeds, so my PS2 figures are dated Steam community guides (2013-2020). The BF4 Viper uses the BF3 infobox figure (330 km/h) as a proxy, and the BF4 ITV has no figure at all. I set judged=false wherever a number was used, even a community or cross-title one, and judged=true only where no number existed (ITV, Sunderer). Other coders may treat the PS2 community numbers and the BF3 proxy as judgement. 6) Two bands sit right at a threshold: the Dunne's method-A ratio is 0.692 (petrol would make it slow), and the ITV's method-B band hinges on whether its BF4 top speed is above or below 100 km/h.
